stem:
Mapfumo Wholesalers in Gweru is preparing its cash budget for May, June and July.

| Month | Sales US\$ | Purchases US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| April | 41,500 | 23,500 |
| May | 45,500 | 27,000 |
| June | 49,000 | 29,500 |
| July | 53,500 | - |

- 40% of sales are for cash. The other 60% are on credit and debtors pay in the month after the sale.
- Purchases are on credit and creditors are paid in the month after the purchase.
- Wages US\$5,200, rent US\$2,400 and general expenses US\$1,850 are paid in cash each month. Depreciation of US\$1,300 a month is included in the general ledger expenses.
- Drawings are US\$2,500 a month.
- A delivery van costing US\$14,200 will be bought and paid for in June.
- A loan repayment of US\$11,500 will be made in June.
- The bank balance on 1 May is US\$4,150.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Prepare the cash budget for May, June and July.

points.description: Heading and a column for each month
Wages, rent, general expenses and drawings each month, with depreciation excluded
Van and loan repayment shown in June
Net cash flow and opening and closing balances carried forward correctly

parts.explanation: One mark for each group of lines. Depreciation must not appear in the cash budget.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the bank balance at the end of:

parts.label: (ii)
parts.stem: June (the amount of any overdraft; amount only)

parts.label: (i)
parts.stem: the cash received from customers in June
parts.explanation: Cash sales 40% × 49,000 = 19,600; May credit sales 60% × 45,500 = 27,300; total US\$46,900.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.explanation: Creditors 29,500 + wages 5,200 + rent 2,400 + general expenses 1,850 + drawings 2,500 = US\$41,450.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Creditors 29,500 + wages 5,200 + rent 2,400 + general expenses 1,850 + drawings 2,500 = US\$41,450.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the total cash received from customers in the three months.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Which item is NOT included in the cash budget?

options.content: The loan repayment of US\$11,500 in June

options.rationale: Cash is taken out each month.

parts.label: (f)
parts.stem: The owner will ask the bank for an overdraft for June. Advise Mapfumo Wholesalers on how it could reduce or avoid the overdraft.

points.description: The overdraft of US\$5,950 arises in June because the van and the loan repayment fall in the same month
Delay the van or the loan repayment, or buy the van on instalments or lease it
Reduce drawings or ask debtors to pay sooner (discounts) or creditors for longer credit
The overdraft is short, as July restores a positive balance, so a short-term overdraft arranged in advance is a reasonable option

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The overdraft of US\$5,950 arises because the van and the loan repayment both fall in June. The business could delay one of them, lease the van, reduce drawings or collect from debtors sooner. As July returns to a positive balance, a short overdraft arranged in advance is also reasonable.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question prepares a three-month cash budget, calculates balances and gives advice on an overdraft.
hints: Debtors pay a month later; creditors are paid a month later.

stem:
Chipo Garments in Mutare makes school shirts. The standard cost and selling price of one shirt, and the budget for the month, are:

| Standard for one shirt | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Cloth: 1.6 metres at US\$4.25 a metre | 6.80 |
| Labour: 0.75 hours at US\$4.80 an hour | 3.60 |
| Selling price | 18.50 |

Budget: 3,100 shirts sold and fixed costs of US\$9,600. Fixed costs are not absorbed into the standard cost.

Actual results for the month:

| Actual | Amount |
| --- | ---: |
| Shirts made and sold | 3,250 |
| Average selling price | US\$18.20 |
| Cloth used | 5,400 metres, cost US\$23,490 |
| Labour | 2,520 hours, cost US\$12,474 |
| Fixed costs | US\$9,900 |

Use the contribution per shirt for the sales volume variance. Label every variance F (favourable) or A (adverse).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the following variances (amount only; you will state F or A in part (e)):

parts.label: (ii)
parts.explanation: Standard cloth = 3,250 × 1.6 = 5,200 metres. Used 5,400, 200 too many. 200 × US\$4.25 = US\$850 A.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Standard cloth = 3,250 × 1.6 = 5,200 metres. Used 5,400, 200 too many. 200 × US\$4.25 = US\$850 A.

parts.label: (iv)
parts.explanation: Standard hours = 3,250 × 0.75 = 2,437.50. Worked 2,520, which is 82.5 hours more. 82.5 × US\$4.80 = US\$396 A.
parts.workedSolution: 1. Standard hours = 3,250 × 0.75 = 2,437.50. Worked 2,520, which is 82.5 hours more. 82.5 × US\$4.80 = US\$396 A.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Prepare a reconciliation of budgeted profit and actual profit, showing each variance as favourable or adverse.

points.description: Sales volume US\$1,215 F and sales price US\$975 A
Material price US\$540 A and usage US\$850 A
Labour rate US\$378 A, labour efficiency US\$396 A and fixed costs US\$300 A
Actual profit of US\$13,286 agreeing with the actual figures

answerSpec.modelAnswer:
| Reconciliation of budgeted and actual profit | Favourable US\$ | Adverse US\$ | US\$ |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Budgeted profit |  |  | 15,510 |
| Sales volume variance | 1,215 |  |  |
| Sales price variance |  | 975 |  |
| Material price variance |  | 540 |  |
| Material usage variance |  | 850 |  |
| Labour rate variance |  | 378 |  |
| Labour efficiency variance |  | 396 |  |
| Fixed costs spent over budget |  | 300 |  |
| Net variance (adverse) | 1,215 | 3,439 | (2,224) |
| **Actual profit** |  |  | **13,286** |

parts.explanation: One mark for each group of lines. Actual profit = 59,150 - 23,490 - 12,474 - 9,900 = 13,286.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: State whether the two labour variances are favourable or adverse, and suggest one likely cause for them.

points.description: A realistic cause: overtime or a wage rise (rate); untrained workers, poor cloth or machine breakdowns (efficiency)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Both labour variances are adverse. The rate variance may come from overtime or a wage rise, and the efficiency variance from untrained workers, poor cloth or machine breakdowns.

explanation: This ZIMSEC Paper 2 style question calculates the direct and sales variances and reconciles budgeted profit with actual profit.
hints: Standard quantity and hours are for the actual output of 3,250 shirts.
The reconciliation must end at the actual profit.
